title: רבי אסי הכהן

paragraphs: (a) Jerusalem Talmud calls him Yose. Colleague of Ammi the priest; distinguished priests and judges of the Land (see there), ordination, etc.; Yochanan’s students. They carried Sabbath supplies (see Ammi). If Ammi was greater, as discussed there, Avodah Zarah 36b seems opposite: Zeira asked Ammi, Ammi Assi, Assi Yochanan, Yochanan Yannai, Yannai Yonatan ben Amram. Perhaps Yuchasin’s reading. Ours: Zeira suffered difficulty before Assi; Assi before Yochanan; Yochanan before Yannai; Yannai before Natan (should be Yonatan) ben Amram, etc. See Zeira. Thus ours lacks Yuchasin’s “before Ammi, and Ammi.” Ours seems right: Assi taught Zeira, who calls him teacher in Hassefinah, repeatedly asks and reports him. Chullin 128, end of b: Assi did not enter the study hall. He found Zeira and asked, “What did they say in the study hall?” He replied, “What is difficult for you?” He said, etc. He replied, “It was difficult for me too; I asked Abba bar Mammal, who told me,” etc. Assi told him, “Many times Abba bar Mammal told me, and I said to him,” etc. Shabbat 47, end of a: Zeira from Assi from Yochanan. Zeira asks, “Did Yochanan say so? You reported otherwise,” Eruvin 12a. Yoma 24b prints Rav Assi from Yochanan: should be Rabbi Assi, as 27b, 28a. We find neither Zeira asking Ammi nor Ammi asking Assi; no proof Assi was greater. Tosafot explicitly favors Ammi’s greater standing; see there. They submitted to Rav Huna, Gittin 59b. Gelilot Eretz Yisrael places Rav Ammi and Rav Assi’s study between Tiberias’s pillars and graves in a hillside cave. I think Rabbi Ammi and Rabbi Assi, Yochanan’s Tiberias students, where Yochanan too is buried; Rav Ammi and Rav Assi, Rav’s students, were Babylonian. Since Rabbi/Rav Assi confusion is common, after Rav Assi I arrange their students, colleagues, teachers; choose for yourself.

(b) He fasted repeatedly to see Chiyya the great. Heilprin says a student of Rabbi Yochanan saw heaven fall and Rabbi Assi support it with his hand. In the Yerushalmi, a weaver dreams that a student supports the falling sky and identifies him as Rabbi Yose. Chullin 103, end of b: Elazar called him wonder of the generation, meaning greatest, like “men of wonder.” When Rabbi Yisa died, Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba took on the mourning and received condolences. Those present were served meat and wine. [Heilprin adds a verb for taking something off, without naming the object.] See Jerusalem Talmud, beginning of Mi Shemeto. At his death all the cedars were uprooted. Mo'ed Katan 25b reads “all the trees.” The sages gathered his teachings: Yaakov said in Assi’s name in Mani’s name, etc. Assi in Yochanan’s name, Kiddushin 13, end of a.
